În general, pentru adulți: sub 150 mg/dL este normal; între 150 și 499 este crescut; la 500 sau mai mult avem hipertrigliceridemie severă, iar la 1000 sau mai mult, riscul de pancreatită acută este mare. Oats have a pretty impressive relationship with long-term health. Across several large observational studies, eating oatmeal and whole-grain oats was consistently associated with either better or neutral cardiovascular outcomes.

In one analysis, people eating oatmeal two or more times per week had about a 21% lower risk of coronary heart disease compared with those eating less than once per month. Other research found that greater whole-oat consumption was associated with lower all-cause mortality in both men and women.

These studies can’t prove that oats caused people to live longer. People who eat more oats may also exercise more, eat differently, or have other healthy behaviors. Researchers adjusted for many of these factors, and randomized trials provide additional evidence that oat-derived fibers can improve cardiovascular risk factors like LDL cholesterol.

How to Use This: A reasonable target based on these studies is around 50–75 grams of dry oats at least twice per week. Eating them more frequently may provide additional benefit, but the research doesn’t establish an ideal amount.
